Fixture: 90_upsampling_rgba_16x16_up2.jxl
16x16 RGBA, VarDCT lossy d=1.0, upsampling 2, ec_upsampling 2

Purpose
-------
Rung 1: K.2 upsampling at its smallest expressible size. The image is 16x16
and `upsampling` is 2, so F.1 gives an 8x8 frame -- one varblock, one group,
one LF group, one TOC section. Everything after Annex J then runs on 64 samples
and produces 256, which makes this the rung to read a failure on: there is no
group geometry, no section addressing and no multi-varblock assembly left to
blame.

The alpha channel takes the same factor, so the extra channel is 8x8 too and
its shift relative to the frame grid is zero -- the case where G.1.3's literal
extra-channel sizing and F.2's cumulative one coincide. Fixtures 94 and 95 are
the ones that separate them.

Frame structure, as parsed by JPXL itself (jpxl-decode's own frame-header
reader and FrameGeometry, not by any oracle):

  frame 0  kRegularFrame  kVarDCT  frame 8x8 -> output 16x16
           group_dim 256, 1 group, 1 LF group, 1 TOC section
           upsampling 2; 1 extra channel (kAlpha), ec_upsampling 2, dim_shift 0

Note the two sizes. F.1 divides the frame dimensions by `upsampling`, so the
frame -- and with it every group, LF group, varblock and modular channel -- is
the SMALLER of the two. The larger is what K.1/K.2 produce, after the Annex J
restoration filters have run at the smaller size and before Annex K's features
are drawn and Annex L's colour transforms are applied.

The colour content is the shape the VarDCT, progressive and alpha recipes use:
a smooth left half and a 1-pixel checkerboard right half. The checkerboard
earns its place here specifically -- cjxl downsamples the source before
encoding, so the highest representable spatial frequency is exactly the content
whose upsampled reconstruction differs between K.2 and any other interpolator.
This sidecar does not claim particular varblock transforms were chosen.

The alpha content is deliberately NOT the same shape as the colour: a radial
ramp with a hard-edged fully transparent notch in the top-left quadrant. A
decode that upsampled the alpha channel by the colour channels' factor,
transposed it, shifted it, or dropped it and left zeros therefore cannot
produce a plausible image, and the test asserts the alpha plane is
non-constant before it grades anything.

Grading (18181-3 4.2)
---------------------
Filters are left at cjxl's own choice, so this stream is in 18181-3 Annex A's
ordinary error class rather than the tighter no-filter one:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.02,  RMSE <= 1e-3   (filters enabled)

That is deliberate. K.1 places upsampling AFTER Annex J -- the gaborish
convolution and the edge-preserving filter run at the frame's stored size and
K.2 runs on their output. A fixture encoded with --gaborish=0 --epf=0 cannot
distinguish that order from the opposite one, so these fixtures keep the
filters on and accept the looser budget.

The test grades far inside that budget (peak below 1e-4 on every rung), and
asserts a tighter bound of its own; see e2e_upsampling.rs.

Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream (the committed .npy, or a
fresh djxl decode), never against the original source PNG -- Part 3 conformance
bounds decoder-vs-reference error, not encoder loss against the pre-encode
image. That distinction matters more than usual here: cjxl DOWNSAMPLED the
source before encoding, so the stream cannot reconstruct the source even in
principle.

                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_up_rgba_16x16.png  (723 bytes)
                sha256 b3e357f53ec55644c32dee58ead4c46f030ab1ef67f1535dd8660c2a47e99435
                Synthetic PNG, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-upsampling-fixtures.sh with nothing but the standard
                library -- no third-party image was used, converted or
                consulted, and no image library is involved. PNG rather than
                PNM because PNM has no alpha channel.

  Fixture:      164 bytes
                sha256 e0e6e8248852acd28e26a11ace28f9d89a432d82441c17f48bc639cb825234c7

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy):
    90_upsampling_rgba_16x16_up2.npy  (4174 bytes)
    sha256 113117c52934bb800d9908f9cb5c60f6714e2e98236f9ceff7f5103a351d2d1c
    Committed alongside the fixture (< 100 KB).
    Shape (1, 16, 16, 4) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. The channel count
    includes the alpha channel: djxl interleaves the extra channels after the
    colour ones, which is the same order G.1.3 gives the modular channel list
    and the order jpxl-decode returns its planes in. Readable with
    jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build
    (decode is deterministic per libjxl revision, see PINNED_REVISIONS.txt).

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
